match_note: The file covers only the Communications Physics versions of a manuscript transferred from another Nature journal. The first-round reports and rebuttal refer to v1 content: same title, the measurement method in Sec. S.III with Fraunhofer data in Fig. S4, Eq. (2) for B*, the sentence on B* being consistent with decreasing transparency as gate voltage increases, and the introduction sentence on narrow [34], intermediate [35] or wide [36] contacts, all present in v1. The longitudinal (B parallel to I) diode data R1 highlights are in Supplementary Fig. S4(g), which is not in the v1 PDF. Rounds: Version 0 (R1, R2), Version 1 (R1 new objections, R2 accept), Version 2 (R1 recommends rejection; R2 report empty, with an author note referring to private comments to the editor), Version 3 (a new Reviewer #3 with six clarity points), Version 4 (R3 accepts).

concerns.quote: Since the determination of $I_{c+}$ and $I_{c-}$ relies on an out-of-plane magnetic field to probe Fraunhofer interference, nonreciprocal effects associated with vortex dynamics cannot be fully excluded.
concerns.summary: Vortex dynamics or trapped flux, hinted at by asymmetric higher-order Fraunhofer lobes, could produce part of the measured nonreciprocity.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the methodology described in Section S.III of the Supplementary Information be included in the main text, along with a brief discussion of potential contributions from vortex-induced SDE.
concerns.summary: The critical-current extraction method should move from the Supplement into the main text.

concerns.quote: the novelty may fall short of what is typically expected for this journal. There is no clear breakthrough, striking anomaly, or new conceptual mechanism put forward.
concerns.summary: The work is well executed but may lack the novelty expected for the journal.

concerns.quote: A comparative angular study of $\eta$ at different field magnitudes (e.g., $B_\parallel = 60$ mT vs 125 mT) in Figs. S4(h–i) could provide insight into whether the longitudinal SDE observed is robust or field-dependent.
concerns.summary: The apparent diode effect with field parallel to the current (Fig. S4(g)) may signal radial spin-orbit texture and should be tested with angular studies.

concerns.quote: the final results and the driving mechanism for the observed features is not entirely clear to me.
concerns.summary: The critical-current and diode data point to different mechanisms (orbital vs spin-orbit), and their coexistence or competition needs better discussion.

concerns.quote: it is not clear the sentence when "transparency is decreased while increasing gate voltage", in the section discussing gate voltage dependence of critical currents.
concerns.summary: The statement that junction transparency decreases with increasing gate voltage is unclear.

concerns.quote: Do the authors performed measurements at different temperatures on devices with different W_{sc}?
concerns.summary: No temperature dependence was measured for the devices of different contact width.

concerns.quote: it seems that this is a small increment with respect to already present works in literature and this lowers the motivations of the present work.
concerns.summary: The introduction's framing that prior work already probed narrow, intermediate and wide contacts makes the study look incremental; the motivation should be revised.

concerns.quote: I suggest a revision of the mentioned literature especially about works on SDE with planar Josephson junctions.
concerns.summary: The literature on superconducting diode effect in planar Josephson junctions should be revised.

later_concerns.quote: the "damping factors" $(1 - e^{-W_{\text{sc}}/\xi})$ cancel out, yielding no net dependence on $W_{\text{sc}}$. The fact that Fig. 5 displays a clear $W_{\text{sc}}$-dependence contradicts this
later_concerns.summary: Version 1: by the critical-current model, the diode efficiency should be independent of contact width, contradicting the data.

later_concerns.quote: Any conclusions drawn from Eq. (6) to support orbital mechanism dominance are, therefore, fundamentally unfounded.
later_concerns.summary: Version 1: the optimal-q expression comes from a TI edge-state setting and does not apply here.

later_concerns.quote: The expression for $q_{\text{RZ}}$ on page 9 is manifestly incorrect. It completely neglects the influence of Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC), reducing the effect to a bare Zeeman shift.
later_concerns.summary: Version 1: the Rashba-Zeeman momentum estimate ignores the inner Fermi surface contribution.

later_concerns.quote: due to the “--|” shape of the junction, current flow is not strictly horizontal, particularly, in the vertical segment “|” of "--|", the current carries vertical components and hence the Dresselhaus SOC can play a role.
later_concerns.summary: Version 1: the longitudinal diode effect was dismissed without engaging with Dresselhaus SOC in the T-shaped geometry.

later_concerns.quote: the authors rely on normal reflection to explain one observation, but then apply a theoretical framework that explicitly neglects normal reflection to interpret another.
later_concerns.summary: Version 2: selective, inconsistent use of theory; impact judged marginal.

later_concerns.quote: If the reported longitudinal diode effect is an artifact of measurement, the authors should present error bars and confidence intervals.
later_concerns.summary: Version 2: if the longitudinal signal is an artifact, the robustness of all data above 0.5 T is in doubt.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: What is the value of the width for W_{sc}\rightarrow \infty?
later_concerns.summary: Version 3: define the infinite-width device; reorder figures and make the weak link visible; relate Eq. (1) to maximising over phase difference.

later_concerns.quote: being a finite region naturally introduces confinement effects. Since the seen effects are tied to the variations of such a width, it might be useful to mention possible effects.
later_concerns.summary: Version 3: confinement in the finite contact width and the dirty limit could affect the critical currents.

later_concerns.quote: it is not clear to me if the authors were able to measure nonreciprocal currents in the absence of the applied fields.
later_concerns.summary: Version 3: state whether any nonreciprocity is seen at zero field.
